places.name: Alten Corimont
sources: world/sources/lore/extrapolation/settlement-register.md §2 (Alten Corimont M4: captain of the port; smuggling, transit, salvage, the northern trunk; Hist: NONE)
lore: Lore:Alten Corimont; Lore:All Flags Navy

why.founding: Alten Corimont is a river port east-southeast of the Hatching Pools. It grew into a town by being neutral about cargo. It sits on the back-channels between Stormhold and Thorn. A shallow-draft hull can reach its water. It lies far enough from either customs regime that both regimes use it.
why.siteAdvantages: The port stands on the last navigable water below the northern rim. An oxbow makes a natural basin. Firm banks suit warehousing. A rim road behind the port crosses to Morrowind without passing a post.
why.occupantsMotive: A captain of the port governs by a nailed-up price list. Freeholder crews with no tribe and no tree live here. Dunmer factors work the Morrowind trade. Nord hands work off the northern hulls.
why.pressures: No Hist stands here. A crew lives by the price list and the depth of water. Stormhold's vicecanons want the trade but cannot reach it. Rockpoint downriver failed in trying to undercut the price list.
why.wouldChangeIf: If Stormhold or Thorn made the port lawful, the trade would move elsewhere. If the river silted below the oxbow, the town would become a village in five years.

hardConstraints: navigable water for a shallow-draft hull
sheltered basin off the legal lanes
no Hist within the settlement — fixed by the lore
preferences: an oxbow or confluence basin
deliberately equidistant from two customs regimes
a rim road behind it that avoids every post

why.pressures: The racks are full from the wet season through to the dry. A town with no Hist buries its dead elsewhere.

why.siteAdvantages: The rise is firm ground well above the water. The creek behind it is deep enough to hold a hull. It is shallow enough to turn back a keeled hull.
why.occupantsMotive: Fisher households live here. On about four nights a month they pole the rise as a lay-by. They charge for it.
why.pressures: The lay-by trade is worth more than the fish. The port road runs close. A waiting boat has to be kept out of sight.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the free port's list covered waiting time, Chasecreek would be a fishing hamlet again.
